title: Laser shot synthesis parameters
description: Synthesis parameters for one deterministic sci-fi laser shot (RX / ear-candy one-shot), v0.1 (#416, D-030). STEREO: the rendered audio has shape (n, 2) (float64, columns left / right) and the WAV is a 2-channel PCM file; at stereo_width 0 both channels are identical. Only schema_version and seed are required; an omitted field takes the default named in its description. Out-of-range values are rejected, never clamped. A shot is one swept voice (pitch_start_hz to pitch_end_hz over sweep_ms along sweep_curve) of a selectable `family`, plus optional ring modulation, FM, band-passed noise, crackle, echo and stereo width. All ranges and defaults are PROPOSALS chosen for a wide space, not measured against any reference; they are placeholders until the audio-engineer measures them and the user listens. No claim is made about how any family sounds.
$comment: Contract rules. (1) Families (`family`), the 'dimensions' of D-030. They share ONE parameter space; a family changes the oscillator and how it is modulated, never which fields exist. `pew`: sine carrier. `plasma`: band-limited sawtooth carrier (harmonics below 0.45 * the internal rate only). `ion`: sine plus two inharmonic upper partials (ratios 2.003 and 3.01, relative levels 0.5 and 0.25). `rift`: two sine carriers, one sweeping pitch_start_hz to pitch_end_hz and the other pitch_end_hz to pitch_start_hz (mirror sweep), equal level. `subboom`: the sweep voice at 0.5 level plus a sine layer at one quarter of the sweep frequency with a 1.5 times longer decay, 20 Hz high-pass. `glitch`: the sweep voice with its pitch held in `glitch_steps` steps over sweep_ms (sample-and-hold) and an amplitude gate (60 % open, smooth edges) per step. `glitch_steps` has no effect in the other families (like rim f2_ratio at level2 0). (2) Sweep: instantaneous frequency f(t) = pitch_start_hz * (pitch_end_hz / pitch_start_hz) ^ (min(1, t / sweep_ms) ^ sweep_curve); sweep_curve 1 is a pure exponential glide (equal ratio per time), below 1 the pitch moves early, above 1 late. After sweep_ms the pitch holds pitch_end_hz. pitch_end_hz may be above pitch_start_hz (rising shot). Phase is the integral of f, starting at 0. (3) Envelope: linear attack_ms, then exponential decay; decay_ms is the time to fall 60 dB after the attack (same definition as kick amp_decay_ms, rim decay1_ms). The file ends with the shared 5 ms fade-out, the first sample is 0, DC is removed (Hann-shaped bump, as kick / rim). (4) Modulation. fm_amount 0 = off; otherwise the carrier phase is modulated by sin(fm_ratio * carrier phase) with peak index 6 * fm_amount radians, reduced where needed so that carrier plus sidebands stay below 0.45 * the internal rate (anti-aliasing). ring_amount 0 = off; otherwise out = (1 - ring_amount) * x + ring_amount * x * sin(2 pi ring_hz t). (5) noise_level 0 = off; otherwise white noise band-passed at noise_hz (Q 1.2), scaled to unit RMS then to noise_level, times an exponential envelope with half of decay_ms, relative to the voice at unit amplitude. crackle 0 = off; otherwise sparse random impulses (density 1500 * crackle per second, random sign), 2 kHz high-passed, times the same envelope as the noise; in `glitch` crackle additionally detunes each held step by up to +- crackle octaves. (6) variation 0 = off; otherwise pitch_start_hz, pitch_end_hz, sweep_ms and decay_ms are each multiplied by 2 ^ (0.3 * variation * u) with u in [-1, 1] drawn from the seed, then limited to the contract range of that field (a shot sequence with changing seeds varies; the stored parameters stay the requested ones). (7) Echo: echo_mix 0 = off; otherwise feedback delay line of echo_ms and echo_feedback, tap k has level echo_mix * echo_feedback^(k-1); taps that would fall below 1e-4 or past the file end are dropped; with stereo_width above 0 odd taps cross over to the other channel with weight stereo_width (ping-pong). The echo is part of the file length, nothing extends it. (8) stereo_width 0 = both channels identical. Above 0: left / right carrier frequencies differ by +- 15 cents * stereo_width (left up, right down), noise and crackle are mixed per channel as sqrt(1 - w) * common + sqrt(w) * independent, and echo ping-pong as in (7). (9) Rendering is done at twice sample_rate and decimated with a linear-phase Kaiser low-pass; drive uses the kick's anti-aliased saturation on each channel. (10) Peak ceiling: the joint peak of both channels of the QUANTISED file is at most peak_ceiling_dbfs (half an LSB of headroom, as the other categories). polarity is applied after the ceiling. (11) Determinism: same resolved parameters (including seed) give a byte-identical WAV. The seed feeds noise, crackle, variation and glitch detune (own sub-streams); with noise_level 0, crackle 0 and variation 0 the output is seed-independent. (12) Length: the file has exactly round(length_ms * sample_rate / 1000) samples per channel including offset_ms of leading silence (rounded to whole samples). A sound longer than length_ms is cut with the fade. (13) No cross-field rule: every combination of in-range values is valid. The highest carrier is 8000 Hz, so with the anti-aliasing limits of (4) and (9) no field combination needs a rejection. (14) Reject out-of-range values, never clamp. Shared field names keep the meaning of kick-params / rim-params (seed, variants, bpm, sample_rate, bit_depth, drive, polarity, offset_ms, peak_ceiling_dbfs, preset). Engine identity for sidecars: engine.name 'abeltongod-audio-engine-laser' with the laser engine's own version (sample-metadata.schema.json, D-025). The sidecar features are the existing non-pitched ones measured on the mid signal ((L + R) / 2), except peak_dbfs, which is the joint peak of both channels. v0.2 (#425, D-031), points 15-22. (15) Versions and placement. The fields of points 17-21 are declared in the schema_version 0.2 branch of allOf, not in properties (as kick-params v0.3, so a v0.1 sidecar and its resolved form do not change); with schema_version 0.1 unevaluatedProperties rejects them. Every v0.2 field defaults to off / neutral: a 0.2 document that omits them or sets them to their defaults renders the same bytes as the same document at 0.1. length_ms goes up to 6000 ms for 0.2 (the 0.1 branch keeps 3000), room for a salvo and a reverb tail. The resolved form of a 0.2 request carries every v0.2 field; if any tempo sync is used (salvo_rate_mode sync or echo_sync not off) and bpm is absent, the resolved form carries bpm 120 (bpm is otherwise metadata only). (16) Chain order, all after the voice of points 1-6, 8, 9: salvo (17: shots placed, panned and summed) -> echo (7, 20) -> drive -> filter (18, 19) -> reverb (21) -> first sample 0 -> fade-out -> mean removal -> peak ceiling (10) -> offset -> polarity. Everything is applied to the sound of m = file length - offset samples; the offset silence is added at the end. Tails: delay and reverb tails are part of the file length, nothing extends it, and a tail still running at the end is cut by the fade-out (5 ms; 50 ms when reverb_mix is above 0, still raised-cosine, last sample exactly 0), so the file always ends silent. The peak ceiling of point 10 holds over the whole mix including salvo, echo and reverb (it is the last gain stage). Choose length_ms for the tail you want; the contract does not guess it. (17) Salvo (one shot is the default). salvo_count shots, each a full voice (points 1-6, 8, 9) of the same parameters. Shot 0 starts at t = 0; the gap between shot i and shot i + 1 (i = 0 .. count - 2) is base * 2 ^ (-ramp * (2 u_i - 1)) with u_i = (i + 0.5) / (count - 1), where base is, by salvo_rate_mode, `ms`: salvo_spacing_ms; `hz`: 1000 / salvo_rate_hz ms; `sync`: the note length of salvo_sync_note at bpm in ms (a quarter note = 60000 / bpm; 1/8 = half of it, 1/16 a quarter, 1/32 an eighth; T triplet = 2/3, D dotted = 3/2 of the plain value). salvo_rate_ramp > 0 shrinks the gaps from the first to the last (rate rises), < 0 widens them, 0 = equal gaps; ramp has no effect with fewer than 3 shots (one gap) and is no more than a factor 2 per gap. Start times are rounded to whole samples. A shot whose start lies within 10 ms of the end of the sound (or beyond) is dropped, not shortened (like echo taps past the end, point 7). Shot k has pitch_start_hz and pitch_end_hz multiplied by 2 ^ (k * salvo_pitch_step_st / 12) (then limited to the 40 ... 8000 Hz range of those fields, before point 6) and level 10 ^ (k * salvo_level_step_db / 20). Each shot with k >= 1 uses its own sub-seed derived from the seed (noise, crackle, variation and glitch detune differ per shot; shot 0 uses the seed itself, so a one-shot salvo equals the plain shot). salvo_humanize h (seeded; never alters shot 0): the start of shot k moves by u * 0.2 * h * (gap before it) ms, its level by u * 1.5 * h dB and its pitch by u * 0.25 * h semitones, with independent u in [-1, 1] per shot and kind drawn from the seed; the draws of shot k do not depend on salvo_count. Pan: salvo_pan_mode `center` = no panning; `alternate_lr` shot k is at position -w for even k and +w for odd k (left first), `alternate_rl` the reverse; `sweep_lr` the positions go linearly from -w (first) to +w (last), `sweep_rl` from +w to -w, one shot = centre; `random` position w * u per shot drawn from the seed; w = salvo_pan_width. Position p in [-1, 1] (-1 left) is applied to the stereo shot as an equal-power balance: theta = (p + 1) * pi / 4, left gain sqrt(2) * cos(theta), right gain sqrt(2) * sin(theta) (p = 0 is gain 1 on both, p = -1 puts sqrt(2) * left on the left and silence on the right). The echo and the reverb act on the summed, panned salvo. (18) Filter. Applied after drive to the whole stereo mix, same cutoff on both channels. filter_slope 12 = 2nd order, 24 = 4th order (two biquads), Butterworth. hp_hz at its minimum 20 = off, otherwise a high-pass; lp_hz at its maximum 20000 = off, otherwise a low-pass (high-pass first, then low-pass). lp_resonance multiplies the Q of the highest-Q low-pass stage by 1 + 1.5 * lp_resonance (0 = plain Butterworth; no self-oscillation, always stable). Closing sweep: lp_sweep_ms 0 = off; otherwise the low-pass cutoff glides exponentially (equal ratio per time) from lp_hz to lp_sweep_hz over lp_sweep_ms and holds lp_sweep_hz, and the glide restarts at every shot start that is not dropped (so each shot of a salvo is filtered the same way; echo and reverb of the earlier shot meet the restarted cutoff). lp_sweep_hz may be above lp_hz (opening). With the sweep on, lp_hz 20000 is a real start cutoff, not off. The cutoff is updated in blocks of 64 samples with the filter state carried over (a fast sweep is a staircase of 64-sample steps). Filters are linear (they create no aliasing); cutoffs up to 20000 Hz are valid at 44.1 kHz. No cross-field rule: any hp_hz, lp_hz and lp_sweep_hz combination is valid, the result is still peak-normalised (a heavily filtered shot is amplified to the ceiling). (19) Filter and the other v0.1 rules: the 20 Hz high-pass inside the voice (point 1) stays; hp_hz is an extra stage. (20) Delay. The v0.1 echo of point 7 stays; v0.2 adds echo_sync, echo_damp_hz and echo_pingpong, all without effect at echo_mix 0. echo_sync other than `off` replaces echo_ms by the note length of that value at bpm (same table as point 17, rounded to whole samples, at least 1). echo_damp_hz below 20000 low-passes the echo path: tap k (k >= 1) is the dry sum low-passed (k - 1) times by a one-pole low-pass at echo_damp_hz, so later taps get darker and the first tap is not damped. echo_pingpong p in [0, 1] mixes each tap with a hard-alternating version: tap = (1 - p) * tap + p * (sqrt(2) * mid of the tap on the right channel for odd k, on the left for even k, silence in the other channel); with p 0 the v0.1 rule of point 7 (stereo_width crossover) applies unchanged. A tap below 1e-4 or past the end is dropped as in point 7 (the damped taps are not measured for it). (21) Reverb. reverb_mix 0 = off. Otherwise a deterministic algorithmic reverb (a feedback delay network of 8 delay lines with an orthogonal Hadamard mixing matrix, no random numbers, no seed) is added to the signal: output = dry + reverb_mix * wet. The input is the mid signal of the mix delayed by reverb_predelay_ms (whole samples). reverb_size scales the delay lengths between 0.35 and 1.5 times a fixed set of 8 lengths (about 21 ... 62 ms at size 1 for 48 kHz scaled by sample_rate / 48000; the shortest line at size 0 is about 7 ms): a small size is a dense, small space, a large one a spread-out space. reverb_decay_ms is the time for the reverb to fall 60 dB at low frequencies (each line's gain is set from its length); reverb_damp_hz is the corner of a one-pole low-pass in every line, so high frequencies decay faster (20000 = no damping filter beyond the 0 dB at DC). reverb_width 0 = both channels of the wet signal identical, 1 = the two decorrelated outputs of the network (mid / side recombination in between). The wet signal is scaled so that its energy over the whole file (both channels) equals the energy of the dry signal at reverb_mix 1 (reverb_mix is a relative send level; the absolute level is set by the peak ceiling). The reverb is stable for every in-range value (every line gain and damping filter has gain below 1). (22) No cross-field rule except the dropped shots of point 17 and bpm of point 15: every combination of in-range v0.2 values is valid, none is clamped; out-of-range values are rejected as in point 14. Seed independence: with noise_level, crackle, variation and salvo_humanize at 0 and salvo_pan_mode other than `random`, the output is seed-independent (the reverb and all filters use no random numbers).

schema_version.description: 0.1: only the fields under properties (length_ms up to 3000). 0.2 (#425, D-031): may also carry the v0.2 fields (allOf, schema_version 0.2 branch: salvo, filter, delay, reverb) and length_ms up to 6000.

seed.description: Seeds noise, crackle, variation and glitch detune (own sub-streams). Same parameters and seed give a byte-identical WAV.

bpm.description: Context for naming/metadata only, except with schema_version 0.2 and tempo sync (salvo_rate_mode sync, echo_sync): then the tempo; absent = 120 in the resolved form.

length_ms.description: File length including offset_ms (up to 3000 with schema_version 0.1, up to 6000 with 0.2). If shorter than the sound needs, it is cut off and gets a 5 ms fade-out.

pitch_end_hz.description: Carrier frequency after sweep_ms, Hz. May be above pitch_start_hz.

sweep_ms.description: Time from pitch_start_hz to pitch_end_hz, ms.

sweep_curve.description: Exponent of the sweep progress: 1 = pure exponential glide, below 1 early, above 1 late.

attack_ms.description: Linear attack, ms. 0 = the first sample after t = 0 is already at full envelope.

decay_ms.description: Time to fall 60 dB after the attack, exponential.

fm_amount.description: FM index share (peak index 6 * fm_amount rad). 0 = off.

fm_ratio.description: Modulator frequency / carrier frequency. No effect at fm_amount 0.

ring_amount.description: Mix of the ring-modulated signal. 0 = off.

ring_hz.description: Ring modulator frequency, Hz. No effect at ring_amount 0.

noise_level.description: Level of the band-passed noise relative to the voice. 0 = off.

noise_hz.description: Centre of the noise band-pass, Hz. No effect at noise_level 0.

crackle.description: Sparse impulse crackle level and density. 0 = off.

glitch_steps.description: Number of held pitch steps over sweep_ms in the glitch family. No effect in other families.

echo_mix.description: Level of the first echo tap relative to the dry shot. 0 = off.

echo_ms.description: Echo delay, ms. No effect at echo_mix 0.

echo_feedback.description: Level ratio between successive echo taps. No effect at echo_mix 0.

stereo_width.description: 0 = both channels identical; 1 = widest (see contract $comment point 8).

variation.description: Seeded random variation of pitch_start_hz, pitch_end_hz, sweep_ms and decay_ms. 0 = off (then the seed does not change the voice).

drive.description: Anti-aliased saturation, same stage as kick drive. 0 = off.

polarity.description: Sign of the whole output, applied after the peak ceiling.

offset_ms.description: Silence before the sound, rounded to whole samples (as in kick-params).

peak_ceiling_dbfs.description: Joint peak ceiling of the quantised file.

preset.description: Name of the preset these values came from, if any.

salvo_count.description: v0.2. Number of shots in the salvo. 1 = a single shot (the v0.1 behaviour).

salvo_rate_mode.description: v0.2. How the fire rate is given: ms = salvo_spacing_ms, hz = salvo_rate_hz, sync = salvo_sync_note at bpm. No effect at salvo_count 1.

salvo_spacing_ms.description: v0.2. Base gap between shots in mode ms.

salvo_rate_hz.description: v0.2. Shots per second in mode hz (gap = 1000 / rate ms).

salvo_sync_note.description: v0.2. Gap as a note length at bpm in mode sync (T triplet, D dotted).

salvo_rate_ramp.description: v0.2. Fire-rate ramp: above 0 the gaps shrink over the salvo (rate rises), below 0 they widen; 0 = equal gaps. No effect with fewer than 3 shots.

salvo_pan_mode.description: v0.2. Pan pattern over the shots (equal-power); random is seeded.

salvo_pan_width.description: v0.2. Pan excursion: 1 = hard left / right. No effect at salvo_pan_mode center.

salvo_level_step_db.description: v0.2. Level change per shot in dB (shot k: k * step).

salvo_pitch_step_st.description: v0.2. Pitch change per shot in semitones (shot k: k * step).

salvo_humanize.description: v0.2. Seeded random timing, level and pitch deviation of shots 1 and later. 0 = off (then the seed does not change the salvo).

filter_slope.description: v0.2. Filter slope in dB per octave for hp_hz and lp_hz. No effect while both are off.

lp_hz.description: v0.2. Low-pass cutoff, Hz (start cutoff with lp_sweep_ms above 0). 20000 = off unless the sweep is on.

lp_resonance.description: v0.2. Small resonance at the low-pass cutoff (Q of the highest-Q stage times 1 + 1.5 * value). 0 = Butterworth.

lp_sweep_ms.description: v0.2. Duration of the low-pass cutoff glide from lp_hz to lp_sweep_hz, restarted at every shot. 0 = no sweep.

lp_sweep_hz.description: v0.2. Low-pass cutoff at the end of the sweep (held afterwards). No effect at lp_sweep_ms 0.

echo_sync.description: v0.2. Echo time as a note length at bpm instead of echo_ms. off = echo_ms. No effect at echo_mix 0.

echo_damp_hz.description: v0.2. Corner of the one-pole low-pass applied once more to every later echo tap. 20000 = off. No effect at echo_mix 0.

echo_pingpong.description: v0.2. Mix of hard-alternating (odd taps right, even taps left) echo taps. 0 = off. No effect at echo_mix 0.

reverb_mix.description: v0.2. Relative send level of the reverb (1 = wet energy equals dry energy). 0 = off.

reverb_size.description: v0.2. Room size (scales the delay line lengths). No effect at reverb_mix 0.

reverb_decay_ms.description: v0.2. Time for the reverb to fall 60 dB (low frequencies). No effect at reverb_mix 0.

reverb_damp_hz.description: v0.2. High-frequency damping corner inside the reverb, Hz. No effect at reverb_mix 0.

reverb_predelay_ms.description: v0.2. Delay before the reverb starts, ms. No effect at reverb_mix 0.

reverb_width.description: v0.2. 0 = mono wet signal, 1 = widest. No effect at reverb_mix 0.
